validity.researcher_notes:
SUPERSEDED WITHIN THIS BATCH -- see revision below.

ORIGINAL FINDING: The row's ENTIRE sourcing base -- every one of the 9 ref units (Fuel, PipelineType, Status, Capacity, Length, Diameter, StartLocation, EndLocation, Operator, Owner) -- rests on one citation: https://egyptoil-gas.com/reports_category/monthly/page/7/ and /page/2/, described on gem.wiki as 'Monthly Reports - Part 2- November 2024 Edition, retrieved 2026-03-16'. I fetched both URLs directly (curl, browser UA, 200 OK, 184KB each) and confirmed neither page contains the string 'Zeit', 'Gharib', or 'Ras Gharib' anywhere in the HTML. These are not a specific report article -- they are paginated CATEGORY-INDEX pages of Egypt Oil & Gas's monthly-report archive ('Monthly Reports - Part 7' / 'Part 2', a collection-page schema.org type), whose contents are whatever happens to be in that pagination slot on the day it's fetched. As of today (2026-08-27) neither page lists a 'November 2024' edition at all -- newer posts have pushed it off both pages 2 and 7 -- so even the citation's own dateline is no longer reachable from the URL it names. This is a fundamentally unstable, non-permalink citation: it was never a reference TO this pipeline, and would not remain one even if it once coincidentally listed a relevant report title.

Cross-checked the worklist's own existing_ref_checks: Status ('operating') and Capacity/Length (97,000 / 83) all correctly FAILED value-match against both URLs. Diameter ('18') shows 'ok: true, expected content present' -- I verified this is a FALSE POSITIVE: '18' appears on the page only as an ad-zone id ('zoneid=18') and a CSS font-size ('18.0px'), coincidental noise, not a diameter figure. So in fact zero of this row's numeric/status claims are actually supported by the cited page; the automated checker's pass on Diameter should not be trusted here.

Independent verification attempt: WebSearch was unavailable this session (budget exhausted at 200/200 before I could run a query). Bing and DuckDuckGo scraped via curl returned bot-challenge/cached-generic pages regardless of query terms (not usable). Checked Wikipedia (EN) for 'Zeit Bay', 'Zeit Bay oil field', 'Ras Gharib' (exists but does not mention Zeit Bay or any pipeline -- only broad historical/petroleum-center context, and itself flagged by Wikipedia as needing more citations), 'Gulf of Suez Petroleum Company/Corporation' (no article), 'Suez Oil Company' (no article); Arabic Wikipedia 'رأس غارب' (Ras Gharib) mentions only that 'several nearby offshore platforms in the Gulf of Suez feed into its storage tanks' -- generic, no pipeline named, no Zeit Bay connection, no specs. Ran egyptoil-gas.com's own site search for 'Zeit Bay': all hits are 2013-era Dana Petroleum/Zeitco EXPLORATION-WELL news (North Zeit Bay field discoveries tied into the 'Lorcan production facility'), none mention Ras Gharib, a pipeline, or export/transport infrastructure. GEM's own wiki page (read for leads only, never cited) confirms it carries exactly the one broken citation and nothing else -- no start year, no cost, no other refs.

Geographic plausibility: both Zeit Bay and Ras Gharib are real, well-documented Gulf of Suez oil locations (Zeit Bay/Zeitco field cluster in the south near Ras Shukheir/July field; Ras Gharib a historic onshore GPC production center further north), so a coastal crude-gathering line between them is not implausible on its face -- but plausibility is not the same as sourcing, and I could not find ANY document, English or Arabic, that names this specific pipeline, its length, its diameter, or its capacity. Note for context, not concluded as fact: P7975-P7979 (Ras Shukheir-El-Hafair, El-Hafair-Suez, El-Hafair-Musturad x2, Zeit Bay-Ras Gharib) were all entered/updated within one day (2026-03-15/16) and all cite the identical broken egyptoil-gas.com pagination-page pattern -- this looks like a systematic citation-quality defect across that whole micro-batch, not a defect unique to P7979, and is worth flagging up if the other four rows haven't already been separately caught.

No roster match found for a duplicate/relabel -- no other P79xx or P73xx row shares this name or these endpoints, and the Zeit Bay/Ras Gharib corridor doesn't overlap the El-Hafair hub-and-spoke pattern formed by P7975-P7978. Classification (Fuel=Oil, PipelineType=transmission) is plausible for an 18in/97,000bpd trunk but likewise unconfirmed by any source. Recommend: hold at existence/concern, do not treat current values as verified, and route to a follow-up pass with WebSearch available and/or Arabic-language EGPC/PPC annual-report material once budget resets.

REVISION (2026-08-27, batch QC): The EOG crude table names 'Zeit Bay Facilities-Ras Gharib' (Zeit Bay Facilities -> Ras Gharib, 83 km, 18 in) -- exact match to the sheet's length and diameter. This row's own ref leg found and cited that article in this same batch; this validity record was written without it, which is the cross-leg gap documented in the batch note. One item survives unchanged: the table's Capacity cell for this line is '-', so the sheet's 97,000 bpd is still uncorroborated and stays UNRESOLVED.
